SCI-WR-F00-Q01.text: Look at the picture and type the word for what you see.

SCI-WR-F00-Q02.text: What's in this picture? Type its name.

SCI-WR-F00-Q03.text: Have a look at the picture. Type the word that names it.

SCI-WR-F00-Q04.text: Study the picture closely, then type what it is.

SCI-WR-F00-Q05.text: What does this picture show? Type the word.

SCI-WR-F00-Q06.text: What colour is grass? Type your answer in one word.

SCI-WR-F00-Q07.text: How many legs does a bird have? Type your answer.

SCI-WR-T01-Q01.text: Look at the picture. What is it? Type the word.

SCI-WR-T01-Q02.text: What do you see in this picture? Type its name.

SCI-WR-T01-Q03.text: Have a look at the picture, then type the word for what it shows.

SCI-WR-T01-Q04.text: Study the picture. When you know what it is, type the word.

SCI-WR-T01-Q05.text: Name the picture in writing. Type the word as carefully as you can.

SCI-WR-T01-Q06.text: Here is a picture for you. Type the word that names it.

SCI-WR-T01-Q07.text: Which science word goes with this picture? Type it in.

SCI-WR-T01-Q08.text: Type what the picture shows. Check your spelling before you finish.

SCI-WR-T01-Q09.text: Spelling adventure. Look at the picture, work out what it is, and type the word.

SCI-WR-T01-Q10.text: Imagine you're labelling a science poster. What's this picture called? Type the word.

SCI-WR-T02-Q01.text: Use the letter tiles to spell the name of the picture. Drag them into place one by one.

SCI-WR-T02-Q02.text: Can you spell what the picture shows? Drag the letters into the right order.

SCI-WR-T02-Q03.text: Move the letters around until they spell the name of the picture.

SCI-WR-T02-Q04.text: Drag the letters into order to spell the word for the picture.

SCI-WR-T02-Q05.text: Spell the name of the picture with the letter tiles. Think about the sound each letter makes.

SCI-WR-T02-Q06.text: What's in the picture? Spell it by dragging the letters into the right places.

SCI-WR-T02-Q07.text: Say the name of the picture in your head. Then drag the letters to spell it.

SCI-WR-T02-Q08.text: Here are some letters. Put them in the right order to spell what you see in the picture.

SCI-WR-T02-Q09.text: Letter puzzle. Drag the tiles into order to spell the name of what's in the picture.

SCI-WR-T02-Q10.text: Imagine the letters got jumbled in the wind. Put them back in order to spell the picture's name.

SCI-WR-T03-Q01.text: A word is missing a letter. Look at the picture to work out the word, then type the missing letter.

SCI-WR-T03-Q02.text: Which letter is missing from this word? Use the picture to help, then type it.

SCI-WR-T03-Q03.text: Find the gap in the word. The picture tells you what the word is. Type the letter that fills it.

SCI-WR-T03-Q04.text: There is a gap in the word and a picture beside it. Type the missing letter.

SCI-WR-T03-Q05.text: Say the word in your head, sound by sound. Which letter fills the gap? Type it.

SCI-WR-T03-Q06.text: One letter is hiding from this word. Use the picture, then type the one that's missing.

SCI-WR-T03-Q07.text: Read the word with the gap, think about what the picture shows, and type the missing letter.

SCI-WR-T03-Q08.text: A letter has gone missing. Use the picture as your clue and type it in.

SCI-WR-T03-Q09.text: Letter hunt. A letter has wandered off from this word. Look at the picture and type the one that's missing.

SCI-WR-T03-Q10.text: Imagine this word lost a letter on its way to school. Use the picture to work out which one, and type it.

SCI-WR-T04-Q01.text: Think about the colourful outer part of a flower. What is that part called? Type its name.

SCI-WR-T04-Q02.text: A plant has a part that grows underground. What's it called? Type the name.

SCI-WR-T04-Q03.text: Look at the very back of a fish. What do we call that part? Type its name.

SCI-WR-T04-Q04.text: A butterfly has a flat part on its side that it uses for flying. What is that part called? Type its name.

SCI-WR-T04-Q05.text: Which part of a plant stands upright and connects the root to the flower? Type its name.

SCI-WR-T04-Q06.text: Insects have thin feelers on their heads that help them sense the world. What are they called? Type the name.

SCI-WR-T04-Q07.text: A fish has a part near its head that helps it breathe underwater. What's that part called? Type it in.

SCI-WR-T04-Q08.text: At the top of a volcano there's an opening where lava escapes. What's it called? Type the name.

SCI-WR-T04-Q09.text: Deep under a volcano is a hidden pocket where melted rock collects before an eruption. What's it called? Type its name.

SCI-WR-T04-Q10.text: Imagine looking closely at your eye in a mirror. What's the small dark circle right in the centre called? Type its name.

SCI-WR-T05-Q01.text: Your labels are petal, stem and root. Read which one the card asks for, then drag it onto the right part of the flower.

SCI-WR-T05-Q02.text: Which label does the card ask for? Read it, then drag that label onto the right part of the flower.

SCI-WR-T05-Q03.text: You have three labels: wing, antenna and leg. Check which one the card asks for, and drag it to the right part of the butterfly.

SCI-WR-T05-Q04.text: Read the card to see which label you need. Then drag it onto the right part of the fish.

SCI-WR-T05-Q05.text: The labels are stem, root and petal. Drag the one the card names to the middle upright part of the flower.

SCI-WR-T05-Q06.text: Find the label the card mentions, then drag it to the head feeler of the insect.

SCI-WR-T05-Q07.text: Labels ready: gill, tail and fin. Read the card, then drag the one it names to the part of the fish used for breathing.

SCI-WR-T05-Q08.text: Check the instruction on the card, then drag the label it names to the top opening of the volcano.

SCI-WR-T05-Q09.text: Volcano explorer. Your labels are chamber, crater and slope. Drag the one the card names down to the hidden underground pocket.

SCI-WR-T05-Q10.text: Imagine you're labelling a diagram of an eye. Read the card, then drag the label it names to the dark centre.

SCI-WR-T06-Q01.text: This sentence says fish live on the moon. That's not right. Fix it so it's true, and type your new sentence.

SCI-WR-T06-Q02.text: Plants need chocolate to grow? Not quite. Change the sentence so it becomes true, then type it.

SCI-WR-T06-Q03.text: The sentence on the screen says the sun comes out at night. Fix the mistake and type the true version.

SCI-WR-T06-Q04.text: Read the sentence about dogs carefully. It isn't true as written. Change it so it tells the truth, and type your version.

SCI-WR-T06-Q05.text: Something's wrong with this sentence about bees and clouds. Fix it so it's true, then type the whole sentence.

SCI-WR-T06-Q06.text: According to this sentence, your lungs pump blood through your body. Is that right? Fix it so it's true, and type your sentence.

SCI-WR-T06-Q07.text: The sentence says a caterpillar changes into a butterfly inside an egg. Can you fix it so it tells the truth? Type your version.

SCI-WR-T06-Q08.text: Look closely at the sentence about animals and eggs. It's not quite true. Change it so it is, and type your new sentence.

SCI-WR-T06-Q09.text: Imagine a friend wrote this sentence about dolphins in their notebook. It has a mistake. Help them fix it, and type the true sentence.

SCI-WR-T06-Q10.text: Volcano fact check. This sentence about what a volcano releases isn't quite right. Fix it and type the true version.

SCI-WR-T07-Q01.text: Fish live in what? Drag the word that fills the gap: water, fire or clouds.

SCI-WR-T07-Q02.text: Plants need something to grow. Which word completes the sentence: sunlight, chocolate or music? Drag it into the blank.

SCI-WR-T07-Q03.text: The sun comes out during the... what? Your choices are day, night and rain. Drag your pick into the gap.

SCI-WR-T07-Q04.text: A dog is a blank thing. Pick from living, non-living or broken, and drag your choice into the gap.

SCI-WR-T07-Q05.text: Where do bees collect nectar from? Drag the word that completes the sentence.

SCI-WR-T07-Q06.text: Something in your body pumps blood through it. Is it your heart, your lungs or your skeleton? Drag your answer into the blank.

SCI-WR-T07-Q07.text: Where does a caterpillar change? Read the sentence, then drag the word that fills the gap.

SCI-WR-T07-Q08.text: What does ice do when it gets warm? Choose melts, freezes or disappears, and drag it into the sentence.

SCI-WR-T07-Q09.text: Dolphins live in the ocean, but what kind of animal are they? Drag in mammals, fish or reptiles to finish the sentence.

SCI-WR-T07-Q10.text: A volcano can release lava, ash and one more thing. Is it gas, ice cream or music? Drag it into the gap.

SCI-WR-T08-Q01.text: When bees visit flowers, what do they collect? Type your answer in one word.

SCI-WR-T08-Q02.text: Which organ pumps blood around your body? Type it in one word.

SCI-WR-T08-Q03.text: Plants need something from the sky to grow. What is it? Type one word.

SCI-WR-T08-Q04.text: Before a caterpillar becomes a butterfly, it forms a special stage. What's it called? Type one word.

SCI-WR-T08-Q05.text: What do we call an animal that hunts other animals for food? Type your answer in one word.

SCI-WR-T08-Q06.text: Every creature has a natural place where it normally lives. What's that place called? Type one word.

SCI-WR-T08-Q07.text: Breathing in, breathing out. Which organ do you use to do that? Type the word.

SCI-WR-T08-Q08.text: Melted rock that is still underground, not yet erupted, has a special name. What is it? Type it in one word.

SCI-WR-T08-Q09.text: Science word quest. What do we call an animal that has a backbone? Type one word.

SCI-WR-T08-Q10.text: Imagine a whole type of living thing disappears forever. What is that called? Type your answer in one word.

SCI-WR-T09-Q01.text: Dog, cat, bird. What group do all three belong to? Type the group name.

SCI-WR-T09-Q02.text: Apple, banana and grape have something in common. Which group do they belong to? Type it.

SCI-WR-T09-Q03.text: Rose, daisy, tulip. Find what links them and type the name of their group.

SCI-WR-T09-Q04.text: Think about a circle, a square and a triangle. What group are they all part of? Type your answer.

SCI-WR-T09-Q05.text: A lion, a hawk and a shark. What group do all three share? Type the group name.

SCI-WR-T09-Q06.text: A dog, a whale and an elephant all belong to one science group. Which one? Type its name.

SCI-WR-T09-Q07.text: Solid, liquid, gas. What's the name for this group? Type it.

SCI-WR-T09-Q08.text: Evaporation, condensation and precipitation belong together. What group are they part of? Type your answer.

SCI-WR-T09-Q09.text: Check out these three: a thermometer, a ruler and a scale. What group do they belong to? Type it.

SCI-WR-T09-Q10.text: Imagine a frog, a salamander and a newt posing for a group photo. What group are they all part of? Type your answer.

SCI-WR-T10-Q01.text: A butterfly life cycle goes egg, caterpillar, a missing stage, then butterfly. What goes in the gap? Type it.

SCI-WR-T10-Q02.text: A plant starts as a seed, then something happens, then it sprouts and becomes a full plant. What's the missing step? Type it.

SCI-WR-T10-Q03.text: Clouds form, then a step is missing, then puddles form and the sun dries them. What's the missing step? Type it.

SCI-WR-T10-Q04.text: A frog's life cycle goes egg, tadpole, a missing stage, then frog. What happens in the gap? Type it.

SCI-WR-T10-Q05.text: In the water cycle, evaporation comes first, then a missing stage, then precipitation and collection. What's the missing stage? Type it.

SCI-WR-T10-Q06.text: Inside a volcano, pressure builds. Then comes a missing step, before lava flows and cools into rock. What happens in the gap? Type it.

SCI-WR-T10-Q07.text: You get a cut, it bleeds, then something happens before new skin grows. What's the missing step? Type it.

SCI-WR-T10-Q08.text: A scientist asks a question, then does something, then tests it with an experiment and looks at the results. What's the missing step? Type it.

SCI-WR-T10-Q09.text: Follow the energy. The sun reaches a plant, the plant makes food, then a step is missing, and finally an animal uses energy to move. What's missing? Type it.

SCI-WR-T10-Q10.text: Imagine following one drop of water. It evaporates from the ocean, forms clouds and falls as rain. What's the missing final stage? Type it.

SCI-WR-T11-Q01.text: Imagine leaving ice out in the sun. What happens to it? Type your answer.

SCI-WR-T11-Q02.text: A plant gets no water for a long time. What happens to it? Type what you think.

SCI-WR-T11-Q03.text: Picture a glass falling onto a hard floor. What happens? Type your answer.

SCI-WR-T11-Q04.text: What might happen to your teeth if you don't brush them for a long time? Type your answer.

SCI-WR-T11-Q05.text: If you mix blue and yellow paint together, what colour do you get? Type it.

SCI-WR-T11-Q06.text: Someone shakes a fizzy drink bottle, then takes the cap off. What happens? Type your answer.

SCI-WR-T11-Q07.text: If you touch something very hot by accident, what does your hand do? Type what happens.

SCI-WR-T11-Q08.text: A caterpillar has eaten lots of leaves for weeks. What is it getting ready to do? Type your answer.

SCI-WR-T11-Q09.text: Imagine a forest where all the trees are cut down. What's likely to happen to the animals living there? Type your answer.

SCI-WR-T11-Q10.text: Picture a garden with no bees visiting during flowering season. What might happen to the fruit it produces? Type your idea.

SCI-WR-T12-Q01.text: A tray of water goes into the freezer overnight. What do you predict will happen by morning? Type your prediction.

SCI-WR-T12-Q02.text: A seed is planted and watered every day in sunlight. What do you predict will happen over the next few weeks? Type it.

SCI-WR-T12-Q03.text: Imagine a plant kept in a completely dark cupboard for two weeks. What do you predict will happen to it? Type your answer.

SCI-WR-T12-Q04.text: Two identical ice cubes go into two cups: one in a warm room, one in the fridge. What do you predict will happen? Type your prediction.

SCI-WR-T12-Q05.text: A bird builds its nest in a tree right before a big storm is expected. What might happen to the nest? Type your prediction.

SCI-WR-T12-Q06.text: A scientist adds a special fertiliser to only one of two identical plants. What might be different between them after a month? Type your prediction.

SCI-WR-T12-Q07.text: A lunchbox with meat inside is left in a hot car all day. What do you predict about the food by evening? Type your answer.

SCI-WR-T12-Q08.text: Scientists see ice at the poles getting thinner each year, while ocean temperatures rise. If this carries on for decades, what might happen? Type your prediction.

SCI-WR-T12-Q09.text: Imagine a new plant species lands by accident on an island with no natural predators for it. What might happen to its population over time? Type your prediction.

SCI-WR-T12-Q10.text: Two identical plants are grown, one watered daily and one only once a week. Everything else is the same. What do you predict after a month? Type it.

SCI-WR-T13-Q01.text: Look closely at the flower. What do you notice about it? Type your observations.

SCI-WR-T13-Q02.text: What do you notice when you look at this butterfly? Type what you see.

SCI-WR-T13-Q03.text: An ice cube has been in a warm room for ten minutes. What do you notice? Type your observations.

SCI-WR-T13-Q04.text: Picture this plant after two weeks of watering. What do you notice? Type what you observe.

SCI-WR-T13-Q05.text: Two identical cups of water, and one has been left uncovered for a week. What do you notice? Type your observations.

SCI-WR-T13-Q06.text: Compare a plant grown near a window with one grown in a cupboard. What differences do you notice? Type them.

SCI-WR-T13-Q07.text: Imagine watching a caterpillar just before it forms its cocoon. What do you notice? Type your observations.

SCI-WR-T13-Q08.text: Think about the sky right before a thunderstorm. What do you notice? Type what you observe.

SCI-WR-T13-Q09.text: Experiment time. A drop of food colouring goes into a still glass of water, and you watch for one minute. What do you notice? Type it.

SCI-WR-T13-Q10.text: Imagine two plants: one gets plain water, the other gets water with a pinch of salt. After two weeks, what do you notice? Type your observations.

SCI-WR-T14-Q01.text: Why do we wash our hands before eating? Explain in one or two sentences.

SCI-WR-T14-Q02.text: Plants need sunlight. But why? Type your explanation in a sentence or two.

SCI-WR-T14-Q03.text: Ice melts when it is left in the sun. Why does that happen? Explain in one or two sentences.

SCI-WR-T14-Q04.text: When bees visit flowers, it helps plants make seeds. Explain why, in one or two sentences.

SCI-WR-T14-Q05.text: A dolphin lives in the ocean, yet it's a mammal, not a fish. Why? Type your explanation in one or two sentences.

SCI-WR-T14-Q06.text: Why does a caterpillar need to eat so much before it forms a cocoon? Explain your thinking in a sentence or two.

SCI-WR-T14-Q07.text: Why is it dangerous to leave meat out in a hot car all day? Explain in one or two sentences.

SCI-WR-T14-Q08.text: A fair science test only changes one thing at a time. Why do you think that is? Explain in one or two sentences.

SCI-WR-T14-Q09.text: Think about a forest being cut down. Why could it affect animals that don't even live directly in the trees? Explain in one or two sentences.

SCI-WR-T14-Q10.text: Picture scientists testing a new medicine. Why do they try it on many people, not just one, before deciding it works? Explain in a sentence or two.

SCI-WR-T15-Q01.text: What do plants need to grow? Write two or three sentences about it.

SCI-WR-T15-Q02.text: How does a butterfly's life change from start to finish? Write two or three sentences about the butterfly life cycle.

SCI-WR-T15-Q03.text: Why do we wash our hands? Share your ideas in two or three sentences.

SCI-WR-T15-Q04.text: How do bees help plants? Write two or three sentences explaining what you know.

SCI-WR-T15-Q05.text: Write two or three sentences about the water cycle. Try to explain how the water moves.

SCI-WR-T15-Q06.text: Dolphins are mammals, not fish. Write two or three sentences explaining why.

SCI-WR-T15-Q07.text: How does a scientist test an idea fairly? Explain it in two or three sentences.

SCI-WR-T15-Q08.text: Cutting down forests can harm animals that don't even live in the trees. Why? Write two or three sentences.

SCI-WR-T15-Q09.text: Imagine you're explaining to a friend why scientists test new medicines on many people rather than just one. Write two or three sentences.

SCI-WR-T15-Q10.text: What might melting ice at the poles suggest about the Earth's temperature over time? Write two or three sentences.
